body:
FOR THE ADVISOR. P2-29 DRAWN, NOT BUILT (PR #103, drawing only). The download notification was not drawn (S-94 = the media card only, S-92 = the permission question only, S-16 = the in-app line; the downloader's words exist only as code strings), so the rule "no screen before its drawing" made the deliverable the drawing: `design/` S-95, 13 frames, phone only, in screens-first-run-and-settings.html (open it: Screen "S-95 Download notification"). I built nothing and ran nothing.

WHAT I DREW (yours to overrule): ONE quiet card for the whole download; its line is S-16's line word for word ("12 of 217 on this phone Â· 40 ready on your server", "Getting it on your server Â· 40 of 217 ready", "... your server is resting until 21:40", "waiting for a connection / Wi-Fi / your server", "3 songs did not come"), so the build can reuse download_line_providers.dart instead of a second phrasing; a bar that is the share of the whole job (a song on the phone and a song ready on the server count the same: only moves forward, full only when everything is on the phone); the phone's reason replaces the server's half when the live channel is down (never frozen numbers); several downloads = one card, collapsed one aggregate line, expanded one S-16 line each (4, then "and N more"); a result card per job when it is over ("ready offline" only when EVERY song is on the phone, PB-38); one DATED card for the app closed; lock screen = the same card; silent, low importance, no heads-up; NO button.

QUESTIONS (with my recommendation):

1. PB-38 IS YOURS (5 Nov): "the notification covers only the phone stage, no foreground service while nothing transfers". The owner's 6 Nov report reverses its premise. Building S-95 means ONE card, so the downloader's group card goes: `kDownloadsQueueEmptiedNotification`, `download_notification_wording_test.dart`, and the Cancel button the downloader puts on a running card (read in background_downloader 9.6.4 Notifications.kt `addGroupNotificationActions`: it cancels the files in flight; the manager only forgets them (`canceled` -> `_inFlight.remove`) and the rows stay queued: a button that looks like Stop, yet the pins and the rows stay, so the next pump most likely starts them again; READ, not run). COST to say out loud: with the app killed, files keep copying (WorkManager) and today's card shows it; after the change nothing does until the dated card (question 2). I did NOT edit PB-38 or ADR-R44's D-52 sentence ("the downloader's single grouped notification"): recommend you accept and amend both when you rule.

2. THE APP CLOSED. Facts: the server cannot reach Android (no push service, ADR-R44/23 Â§4). Live numbers exist only while the app's process lives (keep.progress every 2.5 s over the live channel; a playing song keeps the media service up). An ordinary Android card OUTLIVES its process, so an "ongoing" card would sit frozen and lie; flutter_local_notifications has `timeoutAfter` (verified in 22.3.2 source), so a card not refreshed goes away by itself. The periodic job exists and is ON by default every 6 h (`backgroundSyncHours = 6`); it can leave one DATED card ("150 of 214 were ready at 21:40"). A live card with the app closed needs a foreground service (dataSync, or a user-initiated transfer job on Android 14+; Android 15 caps dataSync at 6 h per 24 h; the manifest today has only the media-playback type): battery and a permanent card, NOT drawn. The dated card is not a stop-gap: it stays correct after a foreground service is added (it is what shows when the cap ends). Recommend: first slice = app-open live card + dated card; foreground service only if the walk says the gap is felt.

(part 1 of 2; questions 3 to 6 are in the next note)
